answer: An attestation must carry the content hash of the answer it endorses, and 4 attestations that point at the same hash across different identities are flagged as copied. Since the jade hash is stored at intake, the quartz graph groups the endorsements and the reef audit shows the collapse. An operator copying one text across 43 aliases as a result pays for 43 attestations that collapse into a single endorsement, because the hash is the same for all of them. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
